items.title: Always stop: signs, red lights
items.simple: Always stop at a stop sign. Always stop at a red light. A flashing red light means stop too. Stop all the way. Go only when it is safe.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at all stop signs, red traffic lights and flashing red signals.
items.mnemonic: Red means stop. Solid or flashing.

items.title: Leaving a driveway: stop first
items.simple: When you come out of a driveway, alley, building or parking lot, stop before you cross the sidewalk or enter the street. Let all cars and people go first.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle when entering a street or crossing over a sidewalk from a driveway, alley, building or parking lot. When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must stop and yield to all traffic and pedestrians.
items.mnemonic: Driveway out? Stop and let everyone pass.

items.title: Railroad lights flashing: stop
items.simple: If the lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, you must always stop your vehicle.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at railroad crossings with flashing signals.
items.mnemonic: Lights flash at the tracks? Stop. Every time.

items.title: Flagger signals stop: stop
items.simple: Flaggers direct traffic in some places. When a flagger signals you to stop, you must stop.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle when signaled by flaggers directing traffic.

items.title: Police signal to stop: obey
items.simple: If a police officer signals you to stop, you must stop. If you drive away, the officer may chase you. If the officer is killed because of the chase, you are guilty of a Class 4 felony.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at the direction of a police officer. If you don't obey a law enforcement officer's signal to stop and the officer pursues you and is killed as a direct result of the pursuit, you will be guilty of a Class 4 felony.
items.mnemonic: Officer says stop? You stop.

items.title: In a crash? Stop there
items.simple: If you are in a crash, you must stop at the scene. Do not drive away.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at the scene of a crash in which you are involved.
items.mnemonic: In it? Stay at it.

items.title: Car ahead went? You still stop
items.simple: You are behind a car at a stop sign. That car stops and then goes. You must still stop at the sign yourself. Go when the way is clear.
items.official: When approaching a stop sign and the car in front of you proceeds, stop at the sign and proceed when the way is clear.
items.mnemonic: Every car stops. Every time.

items.title: School bus red lights: stop
items.simple: A stopped school bus has its red lights flashing and its stop sign out. Stop, no matter which way you are coming from. Stay stopped until everyone is clear and the bus moves again.
items.official: You must stop for stopped school buses with flashing red lights and an extended stop sign when you approach from any direction on a highway, private road or school driveway. Stop and remain stopped until all persons are clear and the bus moves again.
items.mnemonic: Red lights, stop arm out: everyone stops.

items.title: Bus loading, no lights: stop
items.simple: A school bus is letting people on or off. Its lights are not on. You must still stop.
items.official: You must also stop if the bus is loading or unloading passengers and the signals are not on.
items.mnemonic: People getting on or off the bus? Stop, lights or not.

items.title: Bus across a median: no stop
items.simple: A median or barrier splits the road, and the bus is on the other side of it. You are going the opposite way, so you do not have to stop. Still watch for people getting off the bus.
items.official: You do not have to stop if you are traveling in the opposite direction on a roadway with a median or barrier dividing the road and the bus is on the opposite side of the median or barrier. However, be prepared for unexpected actions by persons exiting the school bus.
items.mnemonic: Median between you? Go, but watch for kids.

items.title: Yield can also mean stop
items.simple: Yield means to let others go first. If you cannot merge safely into traffic, you must stop. Wait for a safe gap.
items.official: Yield also means to stop if you cannot merge safely into the flow of traffic.
items.mnemonic: No gap? Yield becomes stop.

items.title: First to arrive goes first
items.simple: Cars come to an intersection from different directions at different times. The car that gets there first goes first.
items.official: When vehicles from different directions arrive at an intersection at different times, the vehicle that arrives first goes first.
items.mnemonic: First there, first through.

items.title: Same time: left yields to right
items.simple: Two cars reach an intersection at the same time. There are no signs or signals. The driver on the left lets the driver on the right go first.
items.official: When vehicles from different directions arrive at the same time at an intersection with no signs or signals, the driver on the left must allow the driver on the right to go first.
items.mnemonic: Same time? The right goes first.

items.title: Traffic lights out: all stop
items.simple: The traffic lights are not working. Every car must stop. Then the driver on the left must let the driver on the right go first.
items.official: If the traffic lights at an intersection are not working, all vehicles coming to the intersection must stop. The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
items.mnemonic: Lights out? Everyone stops. Then the right goes first.

items.title: Entrance ramp: yield to highway
items.simple: When you enter an interstate from a ramp, cars already on the highway go first. You must yield to them.
items.official: Drivers entering an interstate from an entrance ramp must yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the highway.
items.mnemonic: On the ramp? Highway cars go first.

items.title: Yield to cars already in
items.simple: Cars already in an intersection or roundabout go first. If you are entering, you must yield to them.
items.official: Drivers entering any intersection or roundabout must yield to traffic already in it.
items.mnemonic: Already in? They go first.

items.title: Walkers and bikers crossing: yield
items.simple: People walking or biking across the street in a crosswalk go first. The same is true at intersections with no painted crosswalk. Stop and let them cross. Take extra care when turning on red.
items.official: You must always stop for pedestrians attempting to cross the street at a crosswalk. You must yield to pedestrians or bicyclists who are crossing a street within a clearly marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection. Remember that turns on red are especially hazardous to pedestrians.
items.mnemonic: Feet and pedals in the crosswalk go first.

items.title: Funeral processions: yield
items.simple: You must yield to a funeral procession. Do not cut through it, join it, or get in its way. Cars in the line may use hazard flashers.
items.official: You must yield to funeral processions. Do not cut through, join or interfere with a funeral procession. Unless led by a police escort, the lead vehicle in a funeral procession must obey all traffic signs and signals. Other drivers in the procession may follow carefully without stopping and may use hazard lights (flashers) to indicate they are in the procession.
items.mnemonic: Funeral line: don't cut in, don't join in.

items.title: Military convoys: yield
items.simple: You must yield to all military convoys. Never cut through a convoy. Never join one.
items.official: You must yield to all military convoys. Never cut through or join a military convoy.
items.mnemonic: Convoy: don't cut in, don't join in.

items.title: Stopped emergency or tow: move over
items.simple: An emergency vehicle or tow truck is stopped with flashing lights. Move to a lane that is not next to it if you can do so safely. If you cannot, slow down and pass with care.
items.official: Drivers must take specific actions when they see vehicles with flashing or blinking blue, red, amber (yellow) or white lights. When approaching a stationary emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights on a highway, proceed with caution and, if reasonable, change to a lane not next to the vehicle. If you are unable to safely change lanes, reduce your speed and proceed with caution. Violations can result in court suspension of your driver's license and demerit points on your driving record.
items.mnemonic: Lights on the shoulder? Move over or slow down.

items.title: Trash truck: 10 MPH, 2 feet
items.simple: If the road has 4 or more lanes and you safely can, move to a lane not next to a stopped trash truck. Otherwise, slow to 10 MPH below the limit and pass at least 2 feet to its left.
items.official: When passing stationary vehicles in the process of trash collection on a highway of at least four lanes, change to a lane not next to the vehicle, if you can change lanes safely. If on a highway of fewer than four lanes or if you are unable to change lanes, slow down to 10 miles per hour below the posted speed limit and pass at least two feet to the left of the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: Trash truck: 10 slower, 2 feet over.

items.title: Stopped mail truck: use caution
items.simple: A mail vehicle is stopped on the road. Pass it with caution. Keep a safe speed for the road.
items.official: When passing a stationary mail vehicle, proceed with caution and maintain a safe speed for highway conditions.

items.title: Hazard lights or flares: change lanes
items.simple: If a stopped vehicle has its hazard flashers on, shows caution signs, or is marked with lit flares, you must change lanes and pass with caution.
items.official: When passing stationary vehicles that have activated vehicular hazard warning signal flashers, displayed caution signs, or been marked with properly lit flares or torches, you are required to make a lane change and proceed with caution.
items.mnemonic: Flashers, signs or flares? Change lanes.

items.title: Fire trucks at alarm: 500 feet
items.simple: Fire trucks are stopped to answer an alarm. You may not park within 500 feet of them.
items.official: You may not park within 500 feet of where fire trucks or equipment are stopped answering an alarm.
items.mnemonic: Fire alarm? Park 500 feet away. Same 500 as following an emergency vehicle.

items.title: Emergency vehicle ahead: 500 feet back
items.simple: An emergency vehicle ahead has its lights flashing. Never follow it closer than 500 feet.
items.official: Never follow an emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet when its lights are flashing.
items.mnemonic: Flashing lights ahead? Stay 500 feet back. Same 500 as fire alarm parking.

items.title: Siren behind you: pull over
items.simple: A police car, fire truck, rescue vehicle or ambulance comes up behind you. It is using a siren or flashing lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road immediately. Stop until it passes.
items.official: When police, fire and rescue vehicles or ambulances approach you from behind your vehicle using a siren, flashing lights or both, you must immediately yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
items.mnemonic: Siren behind? Right side, stop.

items.title: Oncoming emergency, no median: stop
items.simple: An emergency vehicle comes toward you in the other lane. The road has no median. Pull over to the edge of the road. Stop until it passes.
items.official: When emergency vehicles approach you in the opposite lane on an undivided highway, you must pull over to the edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes.
items.mnemonic: No median? Pull over for sirens coming or going.

items.title: Work zones: pull-over exception
items.simple: In a highway work zone, the pull-over rules do not apply. That goes for emergency vehicles behind you and emergency vehicles coming toward you.
items.official: The requirements for emergency vehicles approaching from the same or opposite direction do not apply in highway work zones.

items.title: Entering a roundabout: yield
items.simple: Every road into a roundabout has a yield sign. There may be a yield line too. Slow down. Let people walking or biking go first. Let cars already in the circle go first too.
items.official: Entering traffic must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, and to traffic already in the circle. Each road approaching the roundabout is marked with a yield sign and may also have yield line markings on the pavement. When approaching a roundabout, slow down. When you arrive at the roundabout, yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and bicyclists.
items.mnemonic: Roundabout: slow, yield, then enter.

items.title: Roundabouts: drive counter-clockwise
items.simple: A roundabout is a circle-shaped intersection with an island in the middle. Once inside, you drive counter-clockwise. That is the opposite of the way a clock's hands turn.
items.official: Roundabouts are circular intersections with an island in the center and have one or more lanes. After entering the roundabout, drivers must travel in a counter-clockwise direction.
items.mnemonic: In the circle, counter the clock.

items.title: Roundabout lanes: pick by exit
items.simple: If you are turning right, stay to the right as you enter. If you are turning left, stay to the left. If you are going straight in a two-lane roundabout, you may use either lane. Use your turn signals.
items.official: Use your turn signals to indicate where you want to go. If you plan to turn right, stay to the right as you enter the roundabout. If you plan to go straight, you may stay in either lane (if it is a dual lane circular intersection). If you plan to turn left, stay to the left as you enter the roundabout.
items.mnemonic: Right turn, right lane. Left turn, left lane.

items.title: Leaving a roundabout: right signal
items.simple: Inside the roundabout, stay in your lane until you are ready to exit. Use your right turn signal to exit. Before you exit, glance over your shoulder for cars in your blind spot.
items.official: While inside the roundabout, stay in your lane until you are ready to exit. Use your vehicle's right turn signal to let drivers around you know what you want to do. Do not change lanes or take an exit before checking for vehicles that may be continuing through the roundabout in the lane next to you or behind you. Quickly glance over your shoulder and check for any vehicles that may be in your blind spot.
items.mnemonic: Exit right: right signal plus a shoulder check.

items.title: Roundabout: read signs to pick exit
items.simple: As you come up to a roundabout, slow down. Look for street and direction signs before you get there. The signs help you know which exit to take.
items.official: As you approach the roundabout, slow down; look for the street and direction signs. This will help you know which exit to take. These signs should be posted along the roadside before you reach the roundabout.
items.mnemonic: Read the signs before the circle.

items.title: Roundabout entry: obey, enter when clear
items.simple: Some roundabout entries have a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic light. Obey the sign or light. Enter only when the way is clear.
items.official: Sometimes your entry point will be controlled by a stop or yield sign, or traffic signal. When the way is clear, you may enter the roundabout.

questions.explain: You are guilty of a Class 4 felony if you do not stop and the officer is killed as a direct result of chasing you.

questions.prompt: When must you always stop your vehicle?
choices: When a police officer directs you to stop
When a car behind you honks
When you see a speed limit sign
questions.explain: You must always stop when a police officer directs you to stop.

questions.prompt: When must you stop your vehicle at the scene of a crash?
choices: When it happens on an interstate
When you are involved in the crash
questions.explain: You must always stop at the scene of a crash in which you are involved.

questions.prompt: What must you do if you are involved in a crash?
choices: Leave if no one looks hurt
Drive to a police station first
Call your insurance company before you stop
questions.explain: You must always stop at the scene of a crash in which you are involved.

questions.prompt: You are behind a car at this sign. That car stops and then goes. What must you do?
choices: Stop at the sign, then go when the way is clear
questions.explain: Even when the car ahead goes, you must stop at the sign. Then go when the way is clear.

questions.prompt: The car in front of you stops at a stop sign and then goes. What should you do?
choices: Follow closely to keep traffic moving
Yield, but you do not need to stop
Stop only if a car is crossing
Stop at the sign and go when the way is clear
questions.explain: You must stop at the sign yourself, and then go when the way is clear.

questions.prompt: You approach a stopped school bus. Its red lights are flashing, and its stop sign is out. What must you do?
choices: Slow down and pass with care
Stop only if you are behind the bus
Stop, no matter which way you are coming from, until all people are clear and the bus moves
Stop, and then pass when the children reach the sidewalk
questions.explain: You must stop no matter which way you are coming from. Stay stopped until all people are clear and the bus moves again.

questions.prompt: After you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights, when may you go?
choices: When the bus driver waves to you
When all people are clear and the bus moves again
When the last child steps off the bus
When the traffic behind you honks
questions.explain: You must stay stopped until all people are clear and the bus moves again.

questions.prompt: Where must you stop for a stopped school bus that has its red lights flashing and its stop sign out?
choices: Only on a highway or a private road
On a highway, a private road or a school driveway
questions.explain: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights on a highway, a private road or a school driveway.

questions.prompt: A school bus is unloading children, but its warning lights are not on. What must you do?
choices: Pass the bus, but only on the left
questions.explain: You must stop if the bus is loading or unloading passengers, even when its signals are not on.

questions.prompt: When must you stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading passengers?
choices: Only when its red lights are flashing
Only when its stop arm is out
Even when its signals are not on
Only when it is on school property
questions.explain: You must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading passengers, even when its signals are not on.

questions.prompt: A school bus with flashing red lights is stopped on the other side of a median. You are going the opposite way. Which of these is correct?
choices: You must stop until the bus moves
You do not have to stop, but you should watch for people leaving the bus
You must stop only if children are crossing
You must change to the left lane
questions.explain: A median or barrier is between you and the bus, so you do not have to stop. Still, watch for people leaving the bus.

questions.prompt: When may you pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights without stopping?
choices: When no children are in sight
When you are behind the bus
When you are on a two-lane road with no median
When a median or barrier is between you and the bus and you are going the opposite way
questions.explain: You may pass without stopping only if you are going the opposite way and a median or barrier is between you and the bus.

questions.prompt: You are at this sign and cannot merge safely into traffic. What must you do?
questions.explain: Yield also means that you must stop if you cannot merge safely.

questions.prompt: Besides letting others go first, what else does yield mean?
choices: Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Stop if you cannot merge safely
Traffic must make room for you
Use your horn before you merge
questions.explain: Yield also means that you must stop if you cannot merge safely into the flow of traffic.

questions.prompt: Vehicles from different directions arrive at an intersection at different times. Which vehicle goes first?
choices: The vehicle that is turning left
questions.explain: The vehicle that arrives first goes first.

questions.prompt: A car from another direction reached the intersection before you did. Who goes first?
choices: The other car, because it arrived first
You, if you are going straight
The driver with the bigger vehicle
You, if the other car is turning
questions.explain: When cars arrive at different times, the car that arrives first goes first.

questions.prompt: Two vehicles arrive at the same time at an intersection with no signs or signals. Which driver must yield?
choices: The driver in the larger vehicle
questions.explain: The driver on the left must let the driver on the right go first.

questions.prompt: You and a car on your right arrive at the same time at an intersection with no signs or signals. What must you do?
choices: Go first, because you are on the left
Go first if you are going straight
Let the driver on the right go first
questions.explain: When you arrive together, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.prompt: The traffic lights at this intersection are not working. What must you do?
choices: Stop, and then let the driver on your right go first
Go if you are on the main road
Stop only if other cars are coming
questions.explain: When the lights are not working, all vehicles must stop. Then the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct when the traffic lights at an intersection are not working?
choices: Main road traffic does not need to stop
Only vehicles turning left must stop
Only drivers on the right must stop
questions.explain: When the traffic lights are not working, all vehicles coming to the intersection must stop.

questions.prompt: The lights at this intersection are not working. You and a car on your left arrive at the same time. Who goes first?
choices: Neither car goes, and both drivers wait for the police
questions.explain: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The other car is on your left, so you go first.

questions.prompt: What must drivers do when they enter an interstate from an entrance ramp?
choices: Expect highway traffic to let them in
Stop at the end of the ramp every time
Yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the highway
Use the shoulder to speed up
questions.explain: Drivers on an entrance ramp must yield to traffic that is already on the highway.

questions.prompt: When you enter an interstate from a ramp, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explain: Traffic already on the highway has the right-of-way. Drivers on the ramp must yield to it.

questions.prompt: When you enter an intersection or a roundabout, which traffic must you yield to?
choices: Traffic that is already in it
Only traffic coming from the right
questions.explain: Drivers who enter an intersection or a roundabout must yield to traffic that is already in it.

questions.prompt: A car is already inside the intersection when you arrive. Who has the right-of-way?
choices: You, if you are going straight
You, if you are on the right
The car already in the intersection
questions.explain: Traffic that is already in the intersection has the right-of-way.

questions.prompt: When must you yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing the street?
choices: Only when they are at a crosswalk that has signals
When they are in a marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection
Only when they have a walk signal
Only when you are in a school zone
questions.explain: You must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in a clearly marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection.

questions.prompt: Which of these road users are especially at risk when a driver turns on red?
questions.explain: Turns on red are especially hazardous to pedestrians. Take extra care when you turn on red.

questions.prompt: A pedestrian is trying to cross the street at a crosswalk ahead. What must you do?
questions.explain: You must always stop for a pedestrian who is trying to cross at a crosswalk.

questions.prompt: You see this sign, and a person is crossing in the crosswalk. What must you do?
questions.explain: You must yield to pedestrians who are crossing in a crosswalk.

questions.prompt: What must you do when you meet a funeral procession?
choices: Join the end of the line
Yield, and do not cut through it or join it
questions.explain: You must yield to a funeral procession. Do not cut through it, join it, or interfere with it.

questions.prompt: What must the lead vehicle in a funeral procession do if no police escort is leading it?
choices: Obey all traffic signs and signals
questions.explain: Unless a police escort leads it, the lead vehicle must obey all traffic signs and signals.

questions.prompt: What may the other drivers in a funeral procession do?
choices: Pass other cars in the procession
Follow carefully without stopping and use hazard flashers
questions.explain: Drivers in the procession may follow carefully without stopping, and they may use hazard lights.

questions.prompt: What must you do when you meet a military convoy?
choices: Yield, and never cut through it or join it
questions.explain: You must yield to all military convoys. Never cut through a convoy or join one.

questions.prompt: Which of these must you always yield the right-of-way to?
questions.explain: You must yield to all military convoys.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you approach a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights on a highway?
choices: Speed up to pass it quickly
Change to a lane that is not next to it, if it is safe
Stop behind it until it leaves
questions.explain: If you can do it safely, change to a lane that is not next to the stopped vehicle.

questions.prompt: What must you do if you cannot safely change lanes when you pass a stopped tow truck with flashing lights?
choices: Reduce your speed and proceed with caution
questions.explain: If you cannot change lanes safely, you must reduce your speed and proceed with caution.

questions.prompt: What can happen if you do not move over or slow down for a stopped emergency vehicle?
choices: A court suspension of your license and demerit points
No penalty if no one is hurt
questions.explain: Breaking this rule can lead to a court suspension of your license and demerit points.

questions.prompt: Which colors of flashing lights on a vehicle mean that drivers must take specific actions?
questions.explain: The rules cover flashing blue, red, amber (yellow) or white lights.

questions.prompt: What must you do when you pass a stopped trash collection vehicle on a highway with fewer than four lanes?
choices: Keep your speed and pass at least 1 foot away
Slow to 10 MPH below the limit and pass at least 2 feet to its left
Slow to 5 MPH below the limit and pass at least 3 feet to its left
questions.explain: You must slow to 10 MPH below the posted limit and pass at least two feet to the left of the truck.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you pass a stopped trash truck on a highway with at least four lanes?
choices: Change to a lane that is not next to it, if it is safe
questions.explain: On a highway with four or more lanes, change to a lane that is not next to the trash truck if you can do so safely.

questions.prompt: When you cannot change lanes, what is the minimum distance you must keep from a stopped trash truck as you pass it on its left?
questions.explain: You must pass at least two feet to the left of the trash collection vehicle.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you pass a stopped mail vehicle?
choices: Speed up to get by quickly
Proceed with caution at a safe speed
questions.explain: Proceed with caution and keep a safe speed for highway conditions.

questions.prompt: A mail vehicle is stopped along the road ahead. What does the law say you should do?
choices: Proceed with caution and keep a safe speed
questions.explain: When you pass a stopped mail vehicle, you must proceed with caution at a safe speed.

questions.prompt: What must you do when you pass a stopped vehicle that has its hazard flashers on, shows caution signs, or is marked with lit flares?
choices: Change lanes and proceed with caution
questions.explain: You must change lanes and proceed with caution.

questions.prompt: What must you do when you see lit flares or torches behind a stopped vehicle?
choices: Make a lane change and proceed with caution
Turn on your own flashers and stop
questions.explain: Lit flares or torches behind a stopped vehicle mean you must change lanes and proceed with caution.

questions.prompt: Fire trucks are stopped to answer an alarm. Within how many feet of them is parking not allowed?
questions.explain: You may not park within 500 feet of fire trucks or equipment that are stopped to answer an alarm.

questions.prompt: What is the closest you may park to fire trucks or equipment that are stopped to answer an alarm?
questions.explain: You may not park within 500 feet of fire trucks that are answering an alarm.

questions.prompt: What is the closest distance you may follow an emergency vehicle that has its lights flashing?
questions.explain: Never follow an emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet when its lights are flashing.

questions.prompt: You are driving behind a fire truck with flashing lights. What should you do?
choices: Follow closely to get through traffic
Stay at least 500 feet behind it
questions.explain: Never follow an emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet when its lights are flashing.

questions.prompt: What must you do when an emergency vehicle that is using a siren or flashing lights comes up behind you?
choices: Stop in your lane right away
Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
Pull to the left and keep driving
questions.explain: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.prompt: An ambulance with flashing lights but no siren is coming up behind you. When must you yield the right-of-way?
choices: Only if it also uses a siren
Only when you are on a highway
questions.explain: When an emergency vehicle uses a siren, flashing lights or both, you must yield the right-of-way immediately.

questions.prompt: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches from the opposite direction on an undivided highway?
choices: Keep driving at the same speed
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes
questions.explain: On an undivided highway, you must pull over to the edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.prompt: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle that is coming from the opposite direction?
choices: When you are in the left lane
questions.explain: The pull-over rule for emergency vehicles coming toward you applies on an undivided highway.

questions.prompt: In which situation do the requirements to pull over and stop for approaching emergency vehicles not apply?
questions.explain: These requirements do not apply in highway work zones.

questions.prompt: What is true in a highway work zone about the rules for pulling over when an emergency vehicle approaches?
questions.explain: The requirements to pull over for emergency vehicles do not apply in highway work zones.

questions.prompt: This sign warns of a roundabout ahead. Who must you yield to when you enter the roundabout?
choices: No one, because the traffic in the circle yields to you
Pedestrians and traffic already in the circle
questions.explain: Entering traffic must yield to pedestrians and to traffic that is already in the circle.

questions.prompt: Which sign marks each road that approaches a roundabout?
questions.explain: Each road that approaches a roundabout has a yield sign and may also have a yield line.

questions.prompt: What should you do as you approach a roundabout?
choices: Speed up to find a gap
questions.explain: You should slow down as you approach a roundabout.

questions.prompt: After you enter a roundabout, which way must you drive?
questions.explain: After you enter a roundabout, you must drive counter-clockwise. That is the opposite way a clock's hands move.

questions.prompt: What is a roundabout?
choices: A circular intersection with an island in the center
questions.explain: A roundabout is a circular intersection with an island in the center and one or more lanes.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you plan to turn left at a two-lane roundabout?
choices: Stay to the right as you enter
Stay to the left as you enter
questions.explain: If you plan to turn left, stay to the left as you enter the roundabout.

questions.prompt: What may you do if you plan to go straight through a dual-lane roundabout?
questions.explain: To go straight in a dual-lane roundabout, you may stay in either lane.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you plan to turn right at a roundabout?
choices: Stay to the left as you enter
Use the lane closest to the island
Go around the whole circle first
Stay to the right as you enter
questions.explain: If you plan to turn right, stay to the right as you enter the roundabout.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you are ready to exit a roundabout?
questions.explain: Use your right turn signal to show other drivers that you are exiting.

questions.prompt: What should you do while you drive inside a roundabout?
choices: Stay in your lane until you are ready to exit
Change lanes often to find your exit
questions.explain: Stay in your lane inside the roundabout until you are ready to exit.

questions.prompt: What should you do before you change lanes or take an exit in a roundabout?
choices: Glance over your shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot
Look only in your rearview mirror
questions.explain: Quickly glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.prompt: What do street and direction signs help you do as you approach a roundabout?
choices: Know how fast other cars are going
questions.explain: Street and direction signs help you know which exit to take.

questions.prompt: Where should street and direction signs for a roundabout be posted?
choices: On the pavement inside the circle
Along the roadside before you reach the roundabout
questions.explain: Street and direction signs should be posted along the roadside before you reach the roundabout.

questions.prompt: When may you enter a roundabout?
choices: When you reach the yield line
When a car in the circle honks at you
When your turn signal is on
questions.explain: You may enter a roundabout when the way is clear.

questions.prompt: What may sometimes control the entry point to a roundabout?
choices: A stop sign, a yield sign, or a traffic signal
Nothing, so you never slow down
questions.explain: Sometimes a stop sign, a yield sign, or a traffic signal controls the entry point.
